correctness.rationale: The exact cyclic matching expansion yields \(D_k=q_n-(a^2+b^2-1)q_{n-2}+(a^2-1)(b^2-1)q_{k-2}q_{n-k-2}-2ab\cos(n\theta)\). The Chebyshev product relation gives \(D_{k+1}-D_k=\Delta q_{n-2k-2}\), with \(\Delta=(a^2-1)(b^2-1)\). At every angular top eigenvalue, an unweighted principal path on \(n-k\) vertices has top eigenvalue \(2\cos(\pi/(n-k+1))\), strictly above the largest \(q_m\) root, so \(q_m\) remains positive to the right. Monic real-root characteristic polynomials then have strictly ordered largest roots according to the sign of \(\Delta\) for every angle, with equality when \(\Delta=0\). Continuous support gaps imply strict interior containment, and the Perron/triangle argument supplies the radius corollary. The exact finite polynomial and phase checks (39+28) and 7350 numerical comparisons replayed; finite tests are not relied on for universal quantification.

evidence: Chang--Wang (2012) maximizes the *radius* over all permutations and hence covers the endpoint maximizer in some same-side cases, but it does not supply the strict full-range chain for all k.

Chien--Kirkland--Li--Nakazato (2023) Proposition 2.5 is a general comparison criterion in terms of determinant polynomials; the paper treats weight-permutation inclusions through n=6 and leaves the all-n conjecture open (§7).

The new proof derives the explicit difference \(D_{k+1}-D_k=(a^2-1)(b^2-1)U_{n-2k-2}(x/2)\) and independently bounds the angular top eigenvalue above all roots of this correction; neither conclusion is supplied by the general criteria alone.

Preexisting global-radius extrema are acknowledged, and the asserted strict interior inclusion is stronger. A potentially undiscovered general Jacobi rearrangement theorem remains an explicit risk.

value.rationale: This is an exact natural classification for the smallest nontrivial multiple-defect cyclic-shift family. All angular supports, not only the radius, strictly nest, and the direction reverses precisely for opposed weak/strong defects. The proof supplies a structural Chebyshev difference identity and handles the otherwise difficult subcritical eigenvalue region. The classification resolves a motivated structured slice of the open all-size numerical-range permutation-order problem, rather than a routine specialization or marginal finite increment.
